newsitem.title: CANADA: New Bre-X suit also targets stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: New Bre-X suit also targets stock exchange.

text.p: Another class action lawsuit over the scandal at Bre-X Minerals Ltd's Busang gold property was filed Thursday in British Columbia.

The lawsuit names the Toronto Stock Exchange and brokerage Nesbitt Burns Inc., a subsidiary of the Bank of Montreal, as co-defendants along with Bre-X, its officers and directors, lawyer David Klein said.
Bre-X faces at least nine similar lawsuits in the United States and elsewhere in Canada. Nesbitt Burns has already been named in another Canadian case.
It was unclear whether this was the first Bre-X suit to target the Toronto exchange as a defendant and Klein said he was not sure if any other action had done so.
Toronto Stock Exchange officials were not immediately available for comment.
Bre-X's stock collapsed recently and was delisted from Canadian exchanges and Nasdaq after its Indonesian gold discovery -- once touted as the biggest this century -- was revealed to be a hoax.
"We are working with lawyers from across Canada and in the United States in a coordinated effort to recover compensation for shareholders of Bre-X," Klein said.

"This is a case in which everyone from Bre-X Minerals, its directors and officers to brokers and regulators appear to have been so caught up in gold fever that they lost sight of their responsibilities to investors."
Klein filed the suit on behalf of Bill and Anne Williams, a carpenter and school secretary from Surrey, British Columbia, who invested C$53,000 in Bre-X shares.

The Supreme Court of British Columbia will rule whether to certify the suit as a class action on behalf of Bre-X shareholders in the province with a sub-class for shareholders outside British Columbia.
